nigeria.title: Shipping from China to Nigeria | Consolidation & Lagos Receiving | DDNZ
nigeria.desc: Plan supplier consolidation, Nigerian import documents and Lagos or inland receiving. Send cargo details and the delivery address for a shipment-specific review.
nigeria.heading: China to Nigeria: several suppliers, one receiving plan
nigeria.intro:
A useful shipping plan starts with the goods and ends at an agreed handover point. Match each supplier’s cargo-ready date with the Nigerian importer, receiving address and unloading arrangements before comparing freight prices.

DDNZ coordinates the China sourcing and export handoff. Freight execution is handled by Heaven Born within the confirmed shipment scope. Start with your cargo list; the proposed route, available services and included charges need to be confirmed for that shipment.

sections.heading: A mixed retail shipment, planned before collection
sections.body:
**Planning example: cartons from several suppliers for a Lagos buyer**

Suppose a buyer is combining non-powered phone cases and display accessories from different suppliers. One supplier is ready now, another later. The first decision is whether waiting for a combined shipment is better than sending separate batches.

Make one row per product and supplier: exact description, material, quantity, carton count, packed dimensions, gross weight and ready date. State explicitly whether any accessories include a battery, liquid or powered component. A broad label such as “accessories” is not enough to review the goods.

Agree what happens if cartons arrive short, damaged or differently labelled. Repacking can change the dimensions and weight, so use the released packing list for the freight comparison. Compare FCL and LCL on the same cargo data, including consolidation and destination charges.

sections.heading: Choose the receiving point before the vehicle
sections.body:
**Lagos receiving**

A port arrival, warehouse collection and delivery to a buyer’s address are different handovers. Give the exact address, receiving contact, opening hours and unloading method. State whether the buyer will collect or wants a delivery quotation.

**Onitsha, Kano or another inland city**

Add the inland leg as a separate scope. Identify who arranges release, collection, linehaul, local delivery and unloading. Ask how waiting, failed delivery or storage would be charged. A city name alone does not establish service availability.

For buyers supplying Alaba, Computer Village or Ladipo, retain the exact shop or warehouse address in the brief.

sections.heading: Check import readiness before dispatch
sections.body:
Identify the Nigerian importer and its clearance contact before loading. Have them review the product description, intended use, classification and applicable import documents against the actual cargo.

For SONCAP-regulated goods, check the applicable product certification before shipment. SON describes Product Certificates for Form M and SONCAP certification for customs clearance of regulated products. The requirement must be reviewed by product; “general cargo” is not a compliance decision. [SON official guidance](https://son.gov.ng/soncapservice/)

Ask the importer to confirm the current Form M and PAAR workflow and any other agency requirements for this shipment. Keep invoice, packing list, product information and consignee details consistent. Resolve missing documents before dispatch instead of treating their cost or processing time as already included.

sections.heading: Compare the full scope and name each responsible party
sections.body:
Ask the quotation to distinguish:

- China collection, receiving, consolidation, repacking and export handling.
- Main freight, routing, quote validity and the cargo-ready assumptions.
- Destination handling, document fees and any warehouse or deconsolidation charges.
- Import declaration, duties and taxes, with the responsible importer and clearance party identified.
- Collection, inland transport, delivery appointment and unloading.

For each stage, record who arranges it, who pays and what evidence closes the handover. List exclusions and the basis for inspection, waiting, storage or other exceptional charges. Compare totals only when these scopes match.

sections.heading: Place stock around orders, not assumptions
sections.body:
Before splitting stock between Lagos and an inland location, review order cities, leading SKUs, repeat-order frequency and replenishment needs. Compare transport, handling, stock visibility and returns together. A lower storage rate does not by itself mean a lower delivered cost.

If repeat demand supports a trial, compare a small replenishment batch with delivery from the initial receiving point. Confirm the proposed storage operator, location, access and fees separately.

sections.heading: Questions buyers ask
sections.body:
**Can several suppliers be combined?**

Send each supplier’s location, ready date and packing data. The review must check compatibility, handling and document readiness before a combined shipment is confirmed. Late goods may change the best option.

**Does a Lagos quote include delivery to my shop?**

Only if that address and delivery scope are included in the written quote. Confirm collection, local transport, unloading and possible waiting charges before accepting it.

**Can you give a fixed transit time or all-in tax price now?**

A useful estimate needs the cargo, importer, route and receiving scope. Ask for the schedule assumptions, cost inclusions and quote validity; port arrival is not the same milestone as delivery to your address.

sections.heading: Send a usable Nigeria brief
sections.body: Send the product list and packing photos, quantities, packed dimensions and gross weights; each supplier’s city and ready date; the Nigerian receiving address and importer/clearance contact; and any battery, liquid or other special attributes. Add the target receiving date and whether partial shipments or staged deliveries are acceptable.

peru.title: Shipping from China to Peru | Heavy Cargo & Delivery Planning | DDNZ
peru.desc: Prepare China-to-Peru shipments with packed weight, importer details and a clear delivery scope. Compare heavy-cargo costs beyond the ocean freight rate.
peru.heading: China to Peru: match the cargo, importer and delivery plan
peru.intro:
A usable Peru freight quote connects the China pickup with the importer and final receiving address. Provide the packed cargo data first, then compare routing, destination handling and delivery on the same basis.

DDNZ coordinates sourcing and export handoff in China. Heaven Born handles freight execution within the confirmed scope. Callao, Chancay and an inland address are different routing or delivery requests; availability needs review for the shipment.

sections.heading: Ceramic tiles: check weight before comparing LCL prices
sections.body:
**Heavy-cargo planning example · ceramic tiles**

Tile cartons can be compact but heavy. Quote the final packed dimensions and gross weight of each pallet, including the pallet and protective packaging. Confirm stackability and how the supplier and receiver will load and unload them.

For an LCL quotation using W/M with one cubic metre compared against one metric tonne, compare the packed volume with gross kilograms divided by 1,000. The higher figure determines the rating units under that quotation’s terms.

For example, a hypothetical shipment of 3 CBM and 4,500 kg produces 4.5 W/M units on that basis. It does not establish a freight price. Minimum charges, rounding, density limits and origin or destination charges must be checked in the actual quotation.

Compare LCL and FCL using the same pallet list. Check payload and handling limits before assuming that spare container volume means more tiles can be loaded.

sections.heading: Prepare the Peruvian importer and product information
sections.body:
For ordinary import-for-consumption procedures, SUNAT requires the owner or consignee to have an active RUC and not be classified as “no habido.” Limited exceptions exist; do not use an individual-import exception as an assumption for a commercial shipment. [SUNAT import procedure](https://www.sunat.gob.pe/legislacion/procedim/despacho/importacion/importac/procGeneral/despa-pg.01.htm)

Have the importer and customs representative review the product classification and any product-specific restrictions. For tiles, supply the material, intended use, dimensions, finish and technical information available from the supplier. A suggested HS code is a starting point for review.

SUNAT’s procedure lists transport and commercial documents, plus insurance, control or origin documentation where applicable. Prepare consistent cargo and commercial data for that review. If seeking preferential tariff treatment, ask the importer to confirm eligibility and the required origin proof; buying in China alone does not settle the tariff treatment. [SUNAT supporting documents](https://www.sunat.gob.pe/legislacion/procedim/despacho/importacion/importac/procGeneral/despa-pg.01.htm)

sections.heading: Quote six stages, then compare the total
sections.body:
1. **China pickup:** supplier addresses, number of collections, access and lifting needs.
2. **Origin handling:** receiving, consolidation, export documents, terminal or CFS operations and any repacking.
3. **Main freight:** selected mode, routing, schedule assumptions, chargeable basis and quote validity.
4. **Destination handling:** terminal or deconsolidation, document, warehouse and third-party charges.
5. **Import clearance and taxes:** importer, customs representative, included items and excluded amounts.
6. **Final delivery:** exact address, vehicle access, appointment, unloading and waiting terms.

For LCL, request destination charges explicitly rather than comparing only an ocean rate per CBM. Record who arranges and pays for each stage. A quote labelled “door delivery” still needs a named address and a clear responsibility list.

sections.heading: Plan the handover from port to receiving site
sections.body:
Specify whether your request ends at Callao, another proposed gateway such as Chancay, a collection warehouse or your final address. Confirm the gateway against an available sailing and the receiving plan before booking.

For Lima or an inland delivery, send the district or locality, postcode if available, full address, receiving hours and vehicle restrictions. For heavy pallets, state whether a forklift or other unloading equipment is available and who supplies it. Include a contact who can accept the goods and report visible discrepancies.

Distinguish expected departure, port arrival, release and final delivery. The confirmed itinerary and receiving arrangements determine the estimate; a general transit range does not establish a delivery date. Agree who monitors changes and who handles storage or waiting if the handover is delayed.

sections.heading: Keep consolidation and loading records useful
sections.body:
Record each supplier’s arrival, package count and visible packing condition. Resolve shortages or damage before merging the final packing list. Reconcile pallet IDs, quantities, weights and dimensions after any repacking.

For tiles, agree protection for edges, restraint and stacking before loading. Keep the released packing list and loading records tied to the shipment reference. A loading photograph can support a visible-condition check; it cannot by itself establish the destination, customs release or delivery outcome.

sections.heading: Questions buyers ask
sections.body:
**Is the cheapest rate per CBM the cheapest tile shipment?**

Not necessarily. Check the quote’s weight/measure basis, minimums, handling and destination charges against the final pallet list before comparing total costs.

**Can a shipment enter through Chancay instead of Callao?**

Treat it as a route request to review. The carrier option, cargo acceptance, importer arrangements and final delivery cost must be confirmed for the intended shipment.

**Does delivery pricing include import taxes and unloading?**

Check the written inclusions. Identify the importer and declaration party, list taxes and local charges, and state who provides unloading. Do not assume that all these items are included in a destination name or service label.

sections.heading: Send the details for a Peru quote
sections.body:
Provide the product and intended use, proposed HS code if known, quantity, package or pallet count, final packed dimensions and gross weight. Add photos, cargo value, agreed trade term, supplier locations and ready dates. Flag batteries, liquids, magnets or other handling-sensitive attributes where present.

For tiles, include material, size, pallet weight and stackability. Give the importer’s RUC status and clearance contact, proposed gateway, final address and unloading facilities. State the required receiving date and whether it is flexible.
